previous_description: Describes a relationship between API responses and subsequent operations, enabling hypermedia-driven API navigation. Supports HATEOAS design patterns.
definition: A response-scoped descriptor that names a target operation, by operationId or operationRef, and maps values from the current response or request (via runtime expressions or literals) onto that operation's parameters or request body. It is a design-time statement of how one call can follow another. It is not a hyperlink carried in the response payload.

distinguish_from.when: the API itself sends an outbound request to a consumer-supplied URL, rather than describing a follow-up call the consumer may make to an operation in this API
the 'links' are runtime data inside the response body (e.g. HAL _links, JSON:API links objects) whose shape is being described, not an OpenAPI Link Object
the relationship is conveyed by an actual HTTP Link response header (RFC 8288) declared on the response
you are defining the input the target operation accepts, rather than mapping a value from a prior response into that input

code_evidence: A 'links:' map under a response in an OpenAPI YAML/JSON file whose entries carry operationId or operationRef plus parameters using runtime expressions such as '$response.body#/id'
A springdoc/swagger-core @Link annotation inside @ApiResponse(links = ...), or a swagger-php @OA\Link / NestJS equivalent attached to a response definition
Entries under components.links referenced from responses via $ref '#/components/links/<Name>'

attribute_descriptions.name: description
attribute_descriptions.description: Human-readable explanation of the link's purpose and when a client should follow it; CommonMark is allowed, and it should be set whenever the target or parameter mapping is not self-evident.

notes: The outgoing references to api.tag and api.schema have no basis in the Link Object; consider removing them. The 'uses api.server' relationship reflects the Link 'server' field, which is missing as an attribute. Links attach to a Response, not to Responses, so the api.responses→api.link edge is questionable. Modellers may confuse this with HAL-style payload links.
